scales.title: Everyday intensity

anchors.label: Low
anchors.anchor: Subtle; I notice it when I look for it.

anchors.label: Medium
anchors.anchor: Clear; it shares the sip with other sensations.

anchors.label: High
anchors.anchor: It leads the sip or lingers.

scales.guidance: High intensity is not automatically better.

scales.title: Deep intensity
scales.guidance: Use only in Deep mode; intensity remains separate from liking.

scales.title: Finish duration

anchors.label: Quick
anchors.anchor: Most sensations leave soon after the sip.

anchors.label: Lingering
anchors.anchor: Aroma, taste, or mouthfeel stays clearly present.

scales.guidance: A longer finish is not automatically better.

scales.title: Personal style impression

anchors.label: Did not work
anchors.anchor: It did not work for its intended style, for me.

anchors.label: Mostly missed
anchors.anchor: Several parts felt out of place for the intended style.

anchors.label: Worked
anchors.anchor: It generally worked for the intended style.

anchors.label: Worked well
anchors.anchor: The style felt clear and well put together.

anchors.label: Exceptional for style
anchors.anchor: It felt exceptional for the intended style, to me.

scales.guidance: Optional in Deep mode. This is not an objective quality grade.

scales.title: Personal enjoyment

anchors.anchor: Memorable; I would seek it out

scales.guidance: This independent personal rating is never calculated from sensory responses.

descriptors.title: Fruit
descriptors.definition: An aroma or flavor that reminds you of fruit.

descriptors.title: Citrus
descriptors.definition: Bright fruit impressions such as peel, juice, or zest.

descriptors.title: Lemon-like
descriptors.definition: A lemon, lemon-peel, or lemonade association.

descriptors.title: Orange-like
descriptors.definition: An orange, tangerine, or orange-peel association.

descriptors.title: Orchard fruit
descriptors.definition: Fruit impressions such as apple or pear.

descriptors.title: Berry
descriptors.definition: Fresh, cooked, or jam-like berry impressions.

descriptors.title: Stone fruit
descriptors.definition: Fruit impressions such as peach, apricot, plum, or cherry.

descriptors.title: Tropical fruit
descriptors.definition: Fruit impressions such as pineapple, mango, papaya, or coconut.

descriptors.title: Dried fruit
descriptors.definition: Fruit impressions such as raisin, date, or dried apricot.

descriptors.title: Floral
descriptors.definition: An aroma or flavor that reminds you of flowers.

descriptors.title: Fresh blossom
descriptors.definition: A light impression of a freshly smelled flower.

descriptors.title: Perfumed
descriptors.definition: A stronger, perfume-like flower association.

descriptors.title: Tea-floral
descriptors.definition: A soft flower association often found alongside leafy tea aromas.

descriptors.title: Sweet and browned
descriptors.definition: Sweet-smelling or cooked-sugar associations; not a claim that sugar is present.

descriptors.title: Honey-like
descriptors.definition: An aroma or flavor association with honey.

descriptors.title: Caramel-like
descriptors.definition: A browned-sugar or caramel association.

descriptors.title: Dark sugar
descriptors.definition: A dark brown sugar or molasses association.

descriptors.title: Vanilla-like
descriptors.definition: A vanilla aroma association, whether inherent or added.

descriptors.title: Nut and cocoa
descriptors.definition: Aroma or flavor associations with nuts, cocoa, or chocolate.

descriptors.title: Almond-like
descriptors.definition: A mild, sweet nut association.

descriptors.title: Roasted nut
descriptors.definition: A darker toasted-nut association.

descriptors.title: Cocoa
descriptors.definition: An unsweetened cocoa or cocoa-nib association.

descriptors.title: Dark chocolate
descriptors.definition: A dark chocolate aroma or flavor association.

descriptors.title: Grain and malt
descriptors.definition: Aroma or flavor associations with cereal, malt, bread, or toasted grain.

descriptors.title: Fresh grain
descriptors.definition: A mild uncooked grain or cereal association.

descriptors.title: Malt
descriptors.definition: A malt cereal or malted-grain association.

descriptors.title: Bread
descriptors.definition: A fresh bread or bread-crust association.

descriptors.title: Toasted grain
descriptors.definition: A toasted rice, barley, or cereal association.

descriptors.title: Roast and smoke
descriptors.definition: Aroma or flavor associations created by browning, roasting, smoke, or char.

descriptors.title: Toasted
descriptors.definition: A gentle toast association.

descriptors.title: Clear roast
descriptors.definition: A clear roasted aroma without requiring smoke or char.

descriptors.title: Smoky
descriptors.definition: An aroma or flavor association with smoke.

descriptors.title: Charred
descriptors.definition: A dark char or burned-edge association.

descriptors.title: Ashy
descriptors.definition: A dry ash association that may be intentional or unexpected depending on style.

descriptors.title: Green and botanical
descriptors.definition: Aroma or flavor associations with leaves, vegetables, herbs, grass, marine notes, or roots.

descriptors.title: Fresh leaf
descriptors.definition: A fresh leafy or tender-green association.

descriptors.title: Steamed greens
descriptors.definition: An association with steamed spinach, edamame, or similar greens.

descriptors.title: Fresh herb
descriptors.definition: A fresh herb association.

descriptors.title: Grass
descriptors.definition: A fresh-cut or dry grass association.

descriptors.title: Marine
descriptors.definition: An association with nori, sea air, or another marine aroma.

descriptors.title: Root and earth
descriptors.definition: A botanical root or clean earthy association.

descriptors.title: Spice
descriptors.definition: Aroma, flavor, warmth, or cooling associated with spices.

descriptors.title: Warm spice
descriptors.definition: A warming cinnamon-, clove-, or cardamom-like association.

descriptors.title: Pepper-like
descriptors.definition: A black-pepper-like aroma or prickle.

descriptors.title: Cooling
descriptors.definition: A cooling mint- or menthol-like sensation.

descriptors.title: Fermented and savory
descriptors.definition: Tangy, wine-like, vinegar-like, broth-like, or soy-like associations.

descriptors.title: Tangy fermentation
descriptors.definition: A lively fermented-fruit or cultured association.

descriptors.title: Wine-like
descriptors.definition: An aroma association with wine or fermented fruit.

descriptors.title: Broth-like
descriptors.definition: A light broth or savory-water association.

descriptors.title: Earth and wood
descriptors.definition: Aroma or flavor associations with soil, wood, cedar, or tobacco.

descriptors.title: Clean earth
descriptors.definition: A fresh-soil association without a mold implication.

descriptors.title: Dry wood
descriptors.definition: A dry wood or cedar association.

descriptors.title: Milk and additions
descriptors.definition: Sensations clearly connected to confirmed milk, syrup, fruit, spice, or another addition.

descriptors.title: Dairy
descriptors.definition: A milk, cream, or cultured-dairy association.

descriptors.title: Cereal milk
descriptors.definition: A sweet cereal-and-milk association.

descriptors.title: Plant milk
descriptors.definition: A grain, nut, seed, or coconut association from a confirmed plant milk.

descriptors.title: Syrup or sauce
descriptors.definition: A confirmed syrup, sauce, or sweet flavor contribution.

descriptors.title: Added fruit
descriptors.definition: A fruit ingredient or fruit-flavor contribution recorded separately from the base drink.

descriptors.title: Texture
descriptors.definition: How the drink feels physically in the mouth, separate from flavor.

descriptors.title: Silky
descriptors.definition: Fine, smooth movement with little obvious particle sensation.

descriptors.title: Creamy
descriptors.definition: A smooth, rounded, lubricating sensation.

descriptors.title: Chalky
descriptors.definition: A fine dry powder sensation, distinct from larger grit.

descriptors.title: Gritty
descriptors.definition: Clearly noticeable particles or coarse sediment.

descriptors.title: Coating
descriptors.definition: A layer or sensation that stays on the mouth after swallowing.

descriptors.title: Airy foam
descriptors.definition: Light foam with obvious air and larger bubbles.

descriptors.title: Fine foam
descriptors.definition: Foam made of small, even bubbles.

descriptors.title: Dry grip
descriptors.definition: A drying or gripping mouthfeel, not a bitter taste.

descriptors.title: Dry
descriptors.definition: A loss of mouth lubrication after the sip.

descriptors.title: Rough
descriptors.definition: A coarse gripping sensation on the tongue, gums, or cheeks.

descriptors.title: Puckering
descriptors.definition: A stronger tightening or puckering sensation.

descriptors.title: Finish
descriptors.definition: What remains after swallowing: aroma, taste, mouthfeel, or a change over time.

descriptors.title: Fades
descriptors.definition: The sensation gradually becomes quieter.

descriptors.title: Lingers
descriptors.definition: A sensation stays clearly present.

descriptors.title: Blooms
descriptors.definition: A sensation becomes clearer after swallowing.

descriptors.title: Changes
descriptors.definition: The leading sensation becomes something different.

descriptors.title: Builds
descriptors.definition: A sensation becomes stronger across time or repeated sips.

descriptors.title: Unexpected
descriptors.definition: Something that did not fit what you expected for this drink or style.

descriptors.title: Papery or stale
descriptors.definition: A dry paper, cardboard, or stale association.

descriptors.title: Mold-like
descriptors.definition: A mold-like or damp-basement association that may warrant a safety check.

descriptors.title: Metallic
descriptors.definition: A metal-like taste or mouth sensation.

descriptors.title: Chemical
descriptors.definition: A foreign chemical, solvent, cleaning-product, or medicinal association.

criteria.title: Your own words
criteria.prompt: Before the labels, what stands out?
criteria.helper: Your own words are enough. You can also choose not sure yet.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Describe what stands out before seeing suggestions

criteria.title: Aroma before the sip
criteria.prompt: What reaches your nose before the sip?
criteria.helper: Smell near the drink without forcing an answer. Aroma can also return while you sip or breathe out afterward.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Aroma before sipping

criteria.title: Sweet impression
criteria.prompt: How strong is the sweet impression?
criteria.helper: An unsweetened drink can feel sweet. Added sweetness is recorded separately.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Sweet impression intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Sour side
criteria.prompt: How strong is the sour side?
criteria.helper: Sourness is a taste. Bright or lively can describe a broader shape; strength and enjoyment stay separate.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Sour taste intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Bitterness
criteria.prompt: How strong is the bitterness?
criteria.helper: Bitterness is a taste. First record its strength; then decide whether you enjoy how it fits.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Bitter taste intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Umami or savory depth
criteria.prompt: How strong is the savory or broth-like side?
criteria.helper: Umami is a taste. Marine or leafy aromas are separate observations.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Umami taste intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Salty side
criteria.prompt: Is there a salty taste?
criteria.helper: Record the taste itself, not whether it is good or bad. Not present and not sure are different answers.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Salty taste presence

criteria.title: Explore the sip
criteria.prompt: Which broad direction feels closest?
criteria.helper: Start broad, then open one branch at a time. These are possibilities, not expected answers.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Explore broad flavor families and optional specific descriptors

criteria.title: Body
criteria.prompt: How heavy does the drink feel?
criteria.helper: Body is weight, not smoothness or quality.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose the drink's body or weight

options.label: Light
options.helper: Closer to water or tea-like movement.

criteria.title: Texture in motion
criteria.prompt: What does it feel like as it moves?
criteria.helper: Separate thickness from texture. More than one can be true.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose one or more mouth textures

criteria.title: Dry grip
criteria.prompt: A few seconds after the sip, do your cheeks, gums, or tongue feel drier?
criteria.helper: Astringency is a drying or gripping mouthfeel, not bitterness.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Drying or gripping mouthfeel intensity

criteria.title: What remains
criteria.prompt: Ten seconds later, what remains?
criteria.helper: Aroma, taste, and physical feeling can follow different timelines.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose what remains after swallowing

options.label: Taste
options.helper: Sweet, sour, bitter, salty, or umami remains.

options.label: Dry grip
options.helper: A drying or gripping feeling remains.

options.label: Nothing clear
options.helper: Nothing stands out after the sip.

criteria.title: Finish length
criteria.prompt: How long does the clearest sensation stay?
criteria.helper: Long is not automatically better.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Duration of the finish; longer is not automatically better

criteria.title: Temperature change
criteria.prompt: As it changes temperature, what changes for you?
criteria.helper: There is no required answer. Different drinks and people change in different ways.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose sensations that changed as the drink's temperature changed

criteria.title: Integration
criteria.prompt: Do the parts feel joined or separate?
criteria.helper: Integration does not require one ideal ratio or a strong base drink.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How joined or separate the drink's parts feel

options.label: Joined
options.helper: The parts feel like one drink.

options.label: Layered
options.helper: The parts stay distinct in a useful way.

options.label: One part leads
options.helper: One component clearly leads the rest.

criteria.title: What leads
criteria.prompt: Does anything dominate for you?
criteria.helper: Dominant is descriptive, not automatically a flaw.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose whether one sensation dominates

options.label: The lead changes
options.helper: Different sensations lead across the sip.

criteria.title: Anything unexpected
criteria.prompt: Did anything feel unfamiliar or unexpected for this drink?
criteria.helper: Roast, smoke, earth, marine notes, sourness, bitterness, and dryness can be intentional. If you suspect spoilage or contamination, stop drinking and check the drink rather than scoring it lower.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Record an unexpected note or possible safety concern

criteria.title: How sure are you
criteria.prompt: How sure are you about what you noticed?
criteria.helper: This helps Mugshot phrase your snapshot carefully. It does not grade your palate.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Confidence in this tasting observation

criteria.title: Personal style impression
criteria.prompt: How well did this drink work for its intended style?
criteria.helper: Optional. This is your impression, not an objective grade or professional assessment.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Optional personal impression of how the drink worked for its intended style

criteria.title: How it worked for you
criteria.prompt: How did the leading sensation work for you?
criteria.helper: This preference stays separate from how intense the sensation was.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Personal preference for the leading sensation

criteria.title: Mugsy first-sensation check
criteria.prompt: Which sensation arrived first?
criteria.helper: One stable, drink-aware distinction can guide the next sip without scoring it.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: The first sensation you noticed with Mugsy

criteria.title: Your rating
criteria.prompt: How was this drink for you?
criteria.helper: This personal rating stands on its own. Sensory answers never calculate or change it.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Personal enjoyment rating from one to five stars in half-star steps

criteria.title: Crema observation
criteria.prompt: Notice the crema, then stir once if you want. Does the sip itself change?
criteria.helper: Crema can affect aroma release and expectation. It is not a score of espresso quality.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Optional crema observation for espresso

criteria.title: Shape of brightness
criteria.prompt: Does the brighter side feel gentle, juicy, sharp, or not present?
criteria.helper: This describes shape separately from sourness intensity or enjoyment.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Character of the coffee's brighter or sour side

criteria.title: Clarity
criteria.prompt: How easy is it to distinguish the sensations?
criteria.helper: Clear means easy to distinguish, not automatically better.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How easy the coffee's sensations are to distinguish

criteria.title: Roast presence
criteria.prompt: How strongly does roast lead the drink?
criteria.helper: Roast can feel toasted, smoky, charred, or ashy. Stronger is not automatically better.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Roast flavor intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Sediment or fines
criteria.prompt: Do particles or sediment add to the drink, stay neutral, or distract?
criteria.helper: Sediment can be expected in immersion coffee and is not inherently good or bad.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Personal response to coffee sediment or particles

criteria.title: Water and coffee
criteria.prompt: Does it feel intentionally light, open, diluted, or thinner than you wanted?
criteria.helper: Strength and water-coffee integration are separate from quality.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How water and coffee feel together in an Americano

criteria.title: Cold drink style
criteria.prompt: How was this drink prepared?
criteria.helper: Cold-extracted and hot-brewed-then-chilled drinks can taste different. If unknown, that is useful context.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Confirm how the cold coffee was prepared

criteria.title: As ice melts
criteria.prompt: What changes as the ice melts?
criteria.helper: Dilution can change strength, sweetness, aroma, and texture without one required direction.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Changes as ice melts into the drink

criteria.title: Base drink presence
criteria.prompt: How clearly does the coffee or tea base come through?
criteria.helper: A base can intentionally lead, share the drink, or sit quietly. Stronger is not automatically better.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Intensity of the base drink through milk and additions

criteria.title: Milk sweetness
criteria.prompt: How strong is the sweetness you associate with the milk?
criteria.helper: Record confirmed sweetener separately. Milk sweetness and added sweetness can overlap in perception.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Milk sweetness intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Foam texture
criteria.prompt: How does the foam feel?
criteria.helper: Fine, creamy, airy, coarse, stable, and fading are observations, not automatic quality scores.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Select one or more foam textures

criteria.title: Matcha color
criteria.prompt: How would you describe the color?
criteria.helper: Color is an observation. It does not determine whether you will enjoy the matcha.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Describe matcha color without assigning a quality score

criteria.title: Dispersion
criteria.prompt: Does the matcha stay even, clump, or settle?
criteria.helper: Matcha is a suspension. Stirring or whisking can change what you observe.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How evenly matcha powder stays suspended

criteria.title: Powder texture
criteria.prompt: Does the suspension feel silky, fine, chalky, or gritty?
criteria.helper: These can coexist. Texture, bitterness, and dry grip are separate.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Select one or more matcha powder textures

criteria.title: Matcha foam
criteria.prompt: What is the foam like, if there is any?
criteria.helper: Foam amount, bubble size, stability, and personal enjoyment are separate.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Describe matcha foam

criteria.title: Powder dispersion
criteria.prompt: Does the powder stay even, clump, or settle?
criteria.helper: A powdered drink is a suspension. This observation is separate from how much you enjoy it.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How evenly the drink's powder stays suspended

criteria.title: Powder texture
criteria.prompt: Does the suspension feel silky, fine, chalky, or gritty?
criteria.helper: Texture, bitterness, and dry grip are separate observations.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Select one or more powdered drink textures

criteria.title: Hojicha roast
criteria.prompt: Where does the roast sit?
criteria.helper: Roast can bring sweet, nutty, woody, green, smoky, or charred impressions. Darker is not automatically better.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose the hojicha roast character

criteria.title: Green and roast relationship
criteria.prompt: Do green, woody, and roasted sides share the sip, or does one lead?
criteria.helper: Leaf and powdered hojicha can express these differently.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Relationship between green woody and roasted hojicha character

criteria.title: Tea style
criteria.prompt: Which broad style leads this tea?
criteria.helper: Style helps Mugshot show relevant possibilities. It does not set one ideal.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Choose the broad tea style

criteria.title: Across the cup
criteria.prompt: Compared with the first sip, what is different now?
criteria.helper: Aroma, bitterness, and dry grip can follow different timelines. No change is a valid answer.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Changes between the first and later sips of tea

criteria.title: Botanical identity
criteria.prompt: Which ingredient or botanical feels clearest?
criteria.helper: Herbal infusion is not one flavor family. Use the actual ingredient name whenever you can.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Record the clearest botanical or ingredient

criteria.title: Add-in texture
criteria.prompt: How do pearls, jelly, cream, or another add-in feel?
criteria.helper: Name the add-in first. Its texture and your preference stay separate from the tea itself.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Texture of milk tea pearls jelly cream or another add-in

criteria.title: What was added
criteria.prompt: Which parts came from milk, sweetener, flavor, or another addition?
criteria.helper: Keeping additions explicit prevents a vanilla syrup from becoming evidence that the base coffee or tea had inherent vanilla notes.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Confirm which flavors and sensations came from additions

criteria.title: Added sweetness
criteria.prompt: How strong is the added sweetness?
criteria.helper: This stays separate from the drink's inherent sweet impression and from whether you like it.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Added sweetness intensity; high is not automatically better

criteria.title: Ingredient integration
criteria.prompt: Do the base drink, milk, sweetness, and flavors work together for you?
criteria.helper: A flavor-led drink can be intentional. This asks how the parts relate, not whether the base dominates.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: How the base drink and confirmed additions fit together

criteria.title: Sweetener or sauce finish
criteria.prompt: Does the added sweetness or sauce leave a coating or long aftertaste?
criteria.helper: Record what remains, then separately decide whether it worked for you.
criteria.accessibilityLabel: Coating or aftertaste from sweetener or sauce

packs.title: Universal Lens
packs.explanation: The universal offline Lens separates aroma, taste, texture, finish, confidence, and personal enjoyment without assuming a drink style.

packs.title: Espresso Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because the confirmed drink is espresso or an espresso-and-water preparation. Crema remains an observation, not a quality proxy.

packs.title: Brewed Coffee Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because the confirmed drink is brewed coffee. The prompts describe the sip without diagnosing extraction from one sensation.

packs.title: Pour-over Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because the confirmed preparation is pour-over. Clarity means sensations are easy to distinguish, not that the drink is objectively better.

packs.title: Cold Brew Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is cold brew. Mugshot records extraction style and dilution instead of assuming cold brew must be sweeter or less acidic.

packs.title: Milk Coffee Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is a milk coffee. Coffee presence, milk, foam, sweetness, additions, and integration remain separate observations.

packs.title: Matcha Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is straight matcha. Color, aroma, umami, bitterness, dry grip, suspension, foam, texture, and enjoyment remain distinct.

packs.title: Matcha Latte Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is a matcha latte. Matcha character, milk, sweetness, added flavor, texture, and integration are recorded independently.

packs.title: Leaf Hojicha Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is steeped hojicha leaf. Roast, green and woody character, body, dry grip, and finish can vary by style.

packs.title: Powdered Hojicha Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is powdered hojicha. Dispersion, particles, body, roast, bitterness, and dry grip remain separate.

packs.title: Hojicha Latte Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is a hojicha latte. Roast, tea presence, milk, sweetness, powder texture, and additions are recorded separately.

packs.title: Green Tea Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is green tea. Fresh, steamed, pan-fired, floral, marine, umami, bitter, and drying impressions are possibilities, not requirements.

packs.title: Black Tea Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is black tea. Malt, fruit, floral, sweet, bitter, drying, body, and finish observations remain distinct.

packs.title: White Tea Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is white tea. Subtle is not the same as absent, and aged or mature-leaf styles can be fuller.

packs.title: Oolong Tea Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is oolong. Fresh floral, honeyed fruit, and roasted styles are all legitimate starting points.

packs.title: Herbal Infusion Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is an herbal infusion. Mugshot asks for the actual botanical before suggesting ingredient-relevant language.

packs.title: Milk Tea Lens
packs.explanation: Shown because this is milk tea. Tea presence, milk, sweetness, add-in texture, coating, and integration remain separate.

packs.title: Iced or Frozen Overlay
packs.explanation: Shown because the confirmed drink is iced or frozen; dilution and temperature change are factual context, not quality judgments.

packs.title: Milk Overlay
packs.explanation: Shown because milk was confirmed. Mugshot keeps milk character and base-drink character separate.

packs.title: Sweetener Overlay
packs.explanation: Shown because a sweetener was confirmed. Added sweetness remains distinct from the base drink's sweet impression.

packs.title: Flavor Addition Overlay
packs.explanation: Shown because a flavor was confirmed. Ingredient provenance prevents an added flavor from being mislabeled as an inherent base-drink note.

packs.title: Powdered Preparation Overlay
packs.explanation: Shown because the drink uses suspended powder. Particle texture and settling remain independent from taste and enjoyment.
